decision_reason: IAC identifies the FlyDubai Boeing 737-800 fatal accident as commercial air transport and records all 55 passengers and seven crew killed.

reconciliation_evidence.observation: IATA's 2016 global commercial-aviation census includes FlyDubai among the year's fatal jet accidents.

reconciliation_evidence.record: Preliminary Safety Review 2017 / worldwide 2016 CAT aeroplane fatal accidents
reconciliation_evidence.observation: EASA independently identifies the FlyDubai B737-800 Rostov crash among 2016 fatal CAT aeroplane accidents.

location: Dubai International Airport, United Arab Emirates
source_publisher: Air Accident Investigation Sector, General Civil Aviation Authority (GCAA), United Arab Emirates
decision_reason: The UAE AAIS final report classifies UAE521 as an Annex 13 accident, identifies Boeing 777-31H A6-EMW, serial 32700, as a scheduled passenger flight, and records one firefighter fatally injured after the aircraft came to rest; all 300 occupants survived.

reconciliation_evidence.record: Preliminary Safety Review 2017 / worldwide 2016 CAT aeroplane fatal accidents
reconciliation_evidence.observation: EASA's wider fatal CAT-aeroplane review explicitly includes the Emirates B777-300 Dubai accident among 2016 fatal accidents.

methodology_note: IATA's 2016 report states that its fatality count focuses on people onboard and excludes ground fatalities. Therefore IATA fatality totals cannot by themselves exhaust the frozen BSFM target when external fatalities qualify.
